payload.name: Preserve co-participants in extracted events
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when a message reports an event shared by the speaker and another person using inclusive phrases (e.g., 'we', 'my partner and I', 'my friend and I'); extract the memory with all participants included.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source message describes an event or activity involving multiple people through inclusive phrases such as 'we', 'my partner and I', or 'my friend and I', include every named or clearly implied participant in the extracted content.
Do not reduce a plural subject to only the speaker; preserve the joint nature of the event even if the other participant is not named again in later messages.
When another participant is not explicitly named, record their role or relationship (e.g., 'with partner', 'with friend') instead of omitting them from the event memory.

solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction omitted the speaker's travel companion from a joint event memory, so later queries about the companion were unsupported. The abstract mechanism is that extraction summaries often collapse first-person plural statements ('my partner and I', 'we') into the speaker alone. This rule applies to future construction extraction whenever a message reports an activity shared with others, instructing the system to preserve all named or clearly implied participants. It does not apply to CRUD operations or solo-activity memories.
